proposal: Custom Teamwear Workflow: monthly retainer (776BC), 27 November 2026, v4.2
consent: I am authorised to approve this proposal for 776BC. I approve the Custom Teamwear retainer at A$5,000 ex GST per month for an initial term of six months, approximately 85 consulting hours at A$350/hour pooled across the term, then month to month on 30 days’ written notice, with the fee and hours reviewed at six months and every 12 months after that. Each month is invoiced at its start and payable within seven days, on the scope and general terms set out in this proposal. This approved proposal is the agreement for the retainer; no separate Project Management Agreement is required.
scope: Custom Teamwear retainer: six-month initial term, approximately 85 pooled hours, then month to month
payment_milestones: A$5,000 ex GST invoiced at the start of each month, payable within seven days
approval_type: Approval of scope, monthly fee, initial term, payment and general terms; this proposal is the agreement
proposal_text: The outcome A step change in custom teamwear.Designed as one system. Transform how 776BC designs and delivers custom teamwear, so the business can produce more designs, faster, with a recognisable 776BC look. Customers should be able to make a good decision quickly: the right information at the right time, and their teamwear presented as well as it will be made. Done well, this becomes core capability. 776BC can grow custom teamwear without adding the same effort to every order. We will treat the journey as one system: customer brief, concepts, realistic garment views, revisions, approval and production artwork. Design the whole experience first. Then build it in stages alongside the current process, which keeps running until the new one is proven. An ambition to test: a complete customer brief becomes a compelling, realistic collection presentation within 48 hours. Discover will define eligible briefs and quality checks; the pilot will test the target. This is presentation time, not finished garment delivery. The approachDiscover. Design. Develop. Deliver.Then keep improving.One programme in five stages. The direction is set once and each stage ends with a decision. The retainer funds the work month by month, so pace and priorities can change at any decision without renegotiating the engagement. What has changed since v2.0The same plan, funded as a monthly retainer. A fixed amount 776BC can budget for, with everyday adoption of the new workflow built into the work rather than left until the end. 01 | FirstDiscoverDecember 2026Understand the work and agree the priorities.Result: a shared, evidenced view of the current workflow from brief to production handover, its friction points and what success should look like.Next decision: agree the priority workflow, garment set and acceptance tests. 02 | NextDesignJanuary 2027Design the future experience end to end.Result: the future workflow for customers, designers and production, a reviewed clickable prototype, feasibility findings and a staged development plan.Next decision: accept the design work and confirm the working proof. 03 | Stage gateDevelopWorking proof from FebruaryBuild and test a reliable working system.Result: a working proof on a real rowing brief, followed by a build and pilot on live customer briefs.Next decision: approve the build after the proof, then confirm the pilot passes the launch checks. 04 | Stage gateDeliverAfter a successful pilotHelp the team confidently use and own it.Result: training, editable assets and code, operating instructions and a named internal owner.Next decision: accept the handover and resolve critical defects before launch. 05 | OngoingEvolveEach month after launchKeep the workflow improving with the people who use it.Result: a monthly cycle of feedback, usage review and small improvements, so the system keeps pace with the business and the tools.Next decision: at each monthly review, agree the next improvement. Where we startThe whole journey in view.Discover and Design come first.The first two months answer the questions that decide what to build. Priorities and technical feasibility are established through that work, not assumed. Start with one real customer job.Trace a representative historical job from its original brief through revisions, approval and production handover. Use its emails, file versions and the team’s experience to answer three questions. What happens today?Map the people, files, tools, decisions and handovers. Where does the work get stuck?Find missing information, waiting, repeated effort and avoidable corrections. What should we improve first?Agree the most useful improvement and how we will measure its success. Design then sets out the future experience for the customer, the design team and production, and turns the agreed priority workflow into a clickable prototype. Focused technical checks test the critical assumptions before we define the build. The first six monthsA clear goal.Flexible on the way there.By the end of the initial term, 776BC will have an agreed future workflow, a tested prototype and a working proof on a real brief, with the named users already involved. Timing is indicative and moves with inputs, decisions and agreed breaks on both sides. WhenWhat you will haveDecision at the end DecemberDiscoverOutputs 1–2: the workflow map, job timeline, friction register and asset inventory from one traced job, then ranked requirements and acceptance tests.Agree the priority workflow, garment set and acceptance tests JanuaryDesignOutputs 3–4: the future workflow, a clickable prototype reviewed by the team, feasibility evidence and the development plan.Accept the design work and confirm the working proof February–AprilWorking proofOne historical rowing brief taken through concepts, companion styles, front, back and side views and a controlled revision, checked by Design and Production.Accept the working proof MaySix-month reviewThe proof results with the sponsors, a first adoption review and a recommended plan and hours for build, pilot and Deliver.Approve the build and pilot, and set their pace Discover and Design use just over half of the term’s hours, so the early work moves quickly. The rest funds the working proof. If the proof needs more than its lower estimate, the six-month review decides whether to add hours or finish it in month seven. Making it stickBuilt around the peoplewho will use it.A new workflow only creates value when the team uses it every week. Adoption is planned from the start and measured as a result, not left to handover. Name the users early. Jonny as design counterpart, with the people in Sales and Production who will run it day to day. They shape the prototype and test it on real briefs. Design for how they work. Fit the files, tools and habits the team already relies on, so the new way is easier than the old one. Prove it alongside the current process. The existing workflow keeps running until the new one has passed its checks on live briefs. Measure use, not only delivery. Each monthly review looks at who used it, on which jobs, what slowed them down and what to change next. An owner inside 776BC. A named internal owner who can train new staff and decide on changes, supported by OptiFlows through the Evolve stage. Keep earlier work earning its keep. With the lead’s agreement, up to two of the retainer hours each month may go to small refinements of tools OptiFlows has already delivered for 776BC. Unused refinement time does not build up, and larger changes are scoped separately. Investment and next stepA fixed monthly investment. Monthly feeA$5,000ex GST, invoiced monthly Initial term6 monthsthen month to month Capacity~85 hourspooled across the term RateA$350/hourstandard rate A$400 Notice30 daysin writing, either party How the hours workThe six-month commitment earns a rate below our standard A$400/hour. Hours are pooled across the term rather than split evenly, so Discover and Design move quickly. All consulting time counts, including meetings, reviews and preparation, in half-hour units. A short monthly statement shows hours used, hours left, work delivered and the plan for the next month, and we flag it well before the pool runs low. Good for both sides776BC gets a predictable cost it can budget for, early progress and the freedom to change priorities at each review. OptiFlows can reserve the time and front-load the early work with confidence. After six monthsThe retainer continues at A$5,000 ex GST a month, about 14 hours, until either party gives notice. The six-month review sets the pace for build, pilot and Deliver, including a temporary step-up if 776BC wants to reach launch sooner. It is also when we review the fee and hours for the months that follow; any change is confirmed in writing at least 60 days before it applies. To beginApprove by signing below, or by email from an authorised 776BC representative. Then nominate the day-to-day lead and approver, select the historical job and confirm access. The first month starts on an agreed date in early December 2026. Each month is invoiced at its start and payable within seven days; GST is added where applicable. Software, hosting, specialist and travel costs are separate and need 776BC’s written approval first. Review detailed scopeGo to proposal approval → Supporting detailScope, responsibilities and terms.These details form part of the agreement. Expand each section to review them; all sections are included when you save a PDF. Discover: workflow and requirementsOutputs 1–2 · December Output 1. Current workflow and evidenceOne ten-minute questionnaire for up to four staff, covering volumes, tools, time per step and the main frustrations. One shared asset checklist. One recorded 60-minute screen-share walkthrough in which Jonny and Production retrace a real job, including the 2D to 3D step and the design proof. Sales joins the relevant part.Trace one historical job across up to three styles, from original brief to production handover, using its emails and file versions. The findings are documented in four parts:Workflow map: one page with a lane each for the customer, Sales, Design and Production, and a lane for tools and files. Each step shows who does it, the tool, the files in and out, hands-on time and waiting time. Friction points are numbered on the map. The factory handover is mapped from Production’s side.Job timeline: elapsed days for the traced job, split into work and waiting, with each revision round marked. This sets the baseline, or a measurement plan where records are incomplete.Friction register: each friction point with its evidence, how often it occurs, what it costs in time and the likely type of fix.Asset and rules inventory: templates, garment CADs, logos, design-rule documents and file formats, where they live and whether they are editable.The map is delivered as a private web page, with the evidence behind each step. The team reviews the draft in the first weekly review and the client lead confirms the findings. Output 2. Agreed requirements and testsRank improvements by customer value, time saved and practicality. Agree user needs, design-rule examples, the initial garment set, the named users and success measures. Use up to two 20-minute follow-ups only where material questions remain.The approver confirms the written scope and acceptance tests before detailed prototype work. Design: prototype and development planOutputs 3–4 · January Output 3. Prototype and feasibility evidenceA future workflow covering the customer, design and production experience, a clickable prototype of the agreed priority workflow, and comparison of existing software, configured integrations and a custom solution.Design and Production review the feasibility evidence, with demonstrated and unproven capabilities clearly distinguished. Assess options against quality, editability, compatibility, licensing, data handling and cost. Output 4. A defined development planOne 45-minute joint prototype review with up to three staff and one consolidated refinement.Produce review findings, recommended system structure, the scope and required checks for the working proof, and an indicative plan for build, pilot and Deliver in retainer hours. The monthly review supports the next decision. Test the critical connections earlyUp to two focused technical checks, totalling eight consultant hours in the first month, subject to usable files and licensed access. Prioritise editable artwork to accurate garment views and controlled changes across styles. Develop, Deliver and Evolve: indicative effortStage gates · Funded from the retainer These preliminary allowances support planning. Asset readiness and technical findings may materially change them. Each stage is scoped in writing at its stage gate. StageIndicative effortAt the retainer rate, ex GST Discover and Design48 hoursA$16,800 Develop: working proof40–60 hoursA$14,000–21,000 Develop: build and pilot80–120 hoursA$28,000–42,000 Deliver: launch and handover16–24 hoursA$5,600–8,400 What this means for timingThe initial term covers Discover, Design and the working proof. At the standard allowance of approximately 14 hours a month after the term, launch falls around 13 to 18 months from the start. A temporary step-up in hours, agreed at the six-month review, brings it forward. The working proof and pilotThe working proof uses one historical rowing brief: three concepts on a master style, the chosen direction across two companion styles, front, back and side views and one controlled revision. Design and Production check quality, editability, accuracy and repeatability. The live pilot then uses two designers and five suitable briefs, subject to volume, with the manual process retained as a fallback. Deliver and EvolveDeliver provides training, editable assets and bespoke code, account and recovery documentation, a named internal owner and accepted operating instructions. Evolve then uses the retainer hours for feedback, usage reviews and agreed improvements. Planning allowance across the whole programme: A$64,400–88,200 ex GST at the retainer rate, the same as v2.0. This is not an approved build budget. It excludes GST, third-party costs, specialists and event implementation. Working together and accepting the workTeam input · Reviews · Commercial and general terms Focused team input Preparation: James drafts the workflow and requirements for staff to confirm. Role-specific questionnaires take approximately ten minutes per person, excluding file preparation. Existing approved tools can prefill, collate and flag gaps; James checks the synthesis before requirements are accepted. One shared job pack: the original brief, logos, editable Illustrator files, production files, final collection, revision history and available timings, plus any existing 776BC design-rule documents. One nominated owner coordinates the files. Staff time: allow an estimated 8–10 combined staff-hours across Discover and Design for preparation, questionnaires, the walkthrough, prototype review and decisions. Named users then join prototype reviews, the working proof and the pilot. Ownership: Kate and Cam confirm the sponsors, one day-to-day lead, one commercial approver and Design and Production reviewers. Jonny is the proposed design counterpart. Staff are asked how the work happens today; they are not asked to design the solution. Reviews: a weekly 30-minute lead review during Discover and Design, fortnightly after that, and a monthly review with the sponsors covering progress, hours, adoption and the next priority. One shared decision log. Consolidated feedback within three business days; formal acceptance within five. Silence is not approval. AcceptanceOutputs 1–4 are accepted against the descriptions above. Later stages are accepted against the scope and checks agreed in writing at each stage gate. One consolidated feedback round per deliverable and corrections to agreed scope are included. Record blockers and limitations; any material reduction or substitution needs written agreement. A supported recommendation to narrow the scope or stop is a valid result. Retainer basis and changesThe retainer reserves capacity for the programme; it is not a fixed price for it. Hours are for the Custom Teamwear programme; other OptiFlows work for 776BC is quoted separately unless the lead and OptiFlows agree in writing to fund it from the hours. New requests are logged, and the lead chooses whether each one replaces planned work of similar size, waits for a later month or adds hours. When 80% of the term’s hours are used, OptiFlows confirms what the remaining hours will cover. Work beyond the available hours is scheduled into a later month or quoted separately and approved in writing before it starts, at A$350/hour in 0.5-hour units.Unused hours carry forward within the initial term. At its end, up to eight unused hours carry into the next month and the rest lapse; after that, unused hours carry forward one month. If OptiFlows cannot provide agreed time in a month, the shortfall carries forward or is refunded, at 776BC’s choice. Delayed inputs or decisions move the schedule. Existing client access is assumed; paid tests are quoted before commitment. General termsOnce approved, this proposal is the agreement for the Custom Teamwear retainer between 776BC and Optiflows Consulting (ABN 71 155 199 637). It carries the same general terms as our Project Management Agreement of 20 February 2026.Ownership: materials created specifically for 776BC become 776BC’s property once the month in which they were created is paid. Optiflows keeps its pre-existing methods, frameworks, templates and tools.Use of learnings: Optiflows may use general, non-confidential learnings from the work. No confidential information or internal documentation is shared, and any public reference to 776BC needs prior written approval.Confidentiality: both parties keep sensitive business information shared during the engagement confidential.Term and ending: the initial term is six months from the agreed start date, then month to month. Either party may end the retainer on 30 days’ written notice. If 776BC ends it during the initial term, hours used above the fees paid are payable at A$350/hour; if Optiflows ends it, unused prepaid hours are refunded. Work completed to that date is handed over.Fee review: the A$5,000 monthly fee and A$350/hour rate are fixed for the initial term. The fee and the hours it includes are reviewed at the six-month review and every 12 months after that. Any change is confirmed in writing at least 60 days before it applies; if 776BC does not accept it, either party may end the retainer on the usual notice before the change takes effect.Liability: Optiflows’ liability is limited to the fees paid under this agreement, and excludes indirect or consequential loss. The workflow we will exploreCustomer experience · Safeguards · Boundaries The starting ideas follow 776BC’s project brief. Discover will establish which deserve priority. Brief onceBring colours, logos, references, sponsors and garment choices into one guided brief that a customer, salesperson or designer can complete. Explore extracting information from existing emails and files for staff to confirm. Develop conceptsCreate 3–5 starting directions using 776BC design rules, garment templates and approved assets. Build the collectionThe designer selects and refines a master direction, then applies its design language across the selected styles. Show it realisticallyPresent front, back and side garment views that accurately reflect editable artwork and garment construction. Revise consistentlyAssist changes across relevant artwork, garments and presentation views, with the designer checking the result. Approve and produceRecord the customer’s approved version and prepare editable production outputs for Design and Production release. Keep throughoutDesigner judgement, editable artwork, original logo geometry and garment constraints. Design and Production check work before customer or factory release. Customer assets are used with permission through approved services. The current process keeps running while the new workflow is built and proven alongside it. Not included unless agreed in writingPattern drafting, grading, a full 3D library or major asset repair; a full design-library build, large migration or wider integrations; customer self-service; direct consultation with manufacturing partners; and event implementation.Discover includes a brief assessment of an existing-design 3D event showcase using Jordan’s written input where needed. Implementation is quoted separately; live logo personalisation remains a later opportunity. How we will measure successBaselines first · Pilot targets agreed together Speed to marketTime from an agreed complete brief to customer presentation, and from customer approval to production handover. Efficiency and capacityStaff hours, repeated tasks, waiting time and revision effort per comparable job. Customer experienceEase of briefing, reviewing and approving, using customer feedback and avoidable clarification rounds. Design and production qualityAdherence to design rules, accuracy between garment views and editable artwork, and production handovers accepted without correction. AdoptionThe share of eligible briefs run through the new workflow, and how confident the named users are working with it. Commercial performanceQuote-to-order conversion, styles per order and average order value over a suitable period of live use. Agree baselines, measurement methods and pilot targets during Discover and Design. Conversion and order value are longer-term commercial measures. Previous version (v2.0, 18 November 2026)
